newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish banking confidence index hits 4-yr high.
newsitem.headline: Polish banking confidence index hits 4-yr high.

text.p: The business confidence index for the Polish banking sector, compiled monthly by the Pentor institute, rose 2.2 points to an all-time record of 52.5 points, Pentor's president said on Tuesday.
"The banking business confidence indicator based on a survey of 208 bankers, reached in October its highest level in the four-year history of the project," Eugeniusz Smilowski told a news conference.
The monthly survey is commissioned by the Polish Banking Association.
Smilowski also said that the majority of the polled bankers felt confident this year's fast growth in lending would not result in a rise in bad loans and a possible banking crisis.
Last month the central bank president has said an uncontrolled credit expansion might lead to a banking crisis and a rise in real interest rates was needed to contain the fast credit expansion.
"According to 72 percent of the polled bankers the growth in credit will not lead to a banking crisis and higher rates," Smilowski said.
